sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 828 ± 41.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface FACS confirmed plasma-membrane localization of the Rho-tagged receptor; agonist-driven cAMP responses were measured (functional readout reported in the same study), but the specific functional impact of the tag itself versus untagged receptor was not isolated.
sites.rationale: All three ledger lines describe a single construct: full-length Or11g7 (mouse ortholog of OR11H7) with an N-terminal Rho-tag, surface-confirmed by live-cell FACS. No residue number is stated, but the topology landmarks place the N-terminus (residue 1–24) as the only extracellular terminus — the C-terminus (residues 291–314) is intracellular — so the junction is unambiguously insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before M1). There is no signal peptide in the topology, so the tag is not at risk of being cleaved. The 24-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample clearance (>3 residues) from TM1 at residue 25. Mouse ortholog Or11g7 was cloned full-length into pCI with an N-terminal rhodopsin (Rho) tag; surface display was confirmed by FACS with an anti-Rho-tag antibody on live, non-permeabilized HEK293 cells, including under RTP1S co-expression conditions.

sources.claim: The cell-surface localization of Or11g7 was assessed using fluorescent-activated cell sorting (FACS) with an antibody against the N-terminal rhodopsin tag.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) converge on the same construct and the same site: an N-terminal Rho-tag on the mouse ortholog Or11g7. Because Or11g7 is a close ortholog (not the human protein itself), the evidence is indirect and confidence is medium. No ledger line reports any internal loop insertion, C-terminal tag, or any other junction for this protein or its ortholog. The C-terminus (residues 291–314) is intracellular and cannot carry a surface tag. The four extracellular loops (ECL1: 84–97, ECL2: 165–193, ECL3: 262–271, and the N-terminal domain 1–24) are not addressed by any ledger line beyond the N-terminal site, so no internal sites are proposed.
